model_annotation: This diagram, labeled "Abbildung 1: Öffentliche Anlageinvestitionen in Deutschland, 1991 bis 2023," presents the public investment in Germany from 1991 to 2023, comparing gross and net investments as a percentage of GDP across different government levels. The figure consists of two stacked bar charts, both sharing the same horizontal axis representing years from 1991 to 2023 at one-year intervals. The vertical axis for both charts is labeled "% des BIP1" and ranges from -0.5 to 3.5 in increments of 0.5. Chart (a) "Bruttoanlageinvestitionen" displays gross investments, while chart (b) "Nettoanlageinvestitionen" shows net investments. In both charts, bars are stacked and color-coded to represent different levels of government: blue for "Bund" (federal level), pink for "Länder" (states), green for "Gemeinden" (municipalities), and purple for "Gebietskörperschaften insgesamt" (total public authorities), although the latter is not visible in the stacks as it appears to be a line. The gross investment chart shows a general decline over time, with values ranging from approximately 2.4% in 1994 to around 1.3% in 2023 for total gross investments. The net investment chart indicates mostly negative values after 2000, ranging from about 0.7% in 1994 to roughly -0.4% in 2023 for total net investments. A notable peak is observed around 1994-1995 in both charts, coinciding with the "Bahnreform" (rail reform), marked by an arrow. The bars are consistently stacked, with no apparent sorting or highlighting of specific bars.
